exam_scheme.note: Examination consists of three successive stages: Preliminary Examination (Objective screening; under the revised 2026 pattern each paper carries 300 marks with 1/3rd negative marking), Main Examination (Conventional descriptive across 6 compulsory papers totaling 1500 marks), and Interview / Personality Test (185 marks; grand total 1685 marks).

stages.source_label: MPPSC Vigyapti No. 05-01/2025/Chayan-9: Revised Exam Plan & Syllabus State Service Examination 2026

papers.paper_name: General Studies Paper I (सामान्य अध्ययन प्रथम प्रश्न-पत्र)
papers.negative_marking: 1 mark deducted for each incorrect answer (1/3rd penalty; 100 questions of 3 marks each; formula: 3R - W)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Merit score in Paper I determines qualification for Mains Examination shortlist

papers.paper_name: General Aptitude Test Paper II (सामान्य अभिरुचि परीक्षण द्वितीय प्रश्न-पत्र - CSAT)
papers.negative_marking: 1 mark deducted for each incorrect answer (1/3rd penalty; 100 questions of 3 marks each; formula: 3R - W)
papers.qualifying_threshold: 33% minimum qualifying marks for General/UR candidates (99 marks out of 300), and 30% (90 marks out of 300) for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD candidates; marks not counted for State Service Exam merit ranking

stages.source_label: MPPSC Vigyapti No. 05-01/2025/Chayan-9: Revised Exam Plan & Syllabus State Service Examination 2026

papers.paper_name: General Studies Paper I (Part A: History - 150 marks; Part B: Geography - 150 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each Part (A and B) for General candidates (60 marks each); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (45 marks each)

papers.paper_name: General Studies Paper II (Part A: Constitution, Governance, Political & Administrative Structure - 150 marks; Part B: Social Structure, Education, Health - 150 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each Part (A and B) for General candidates (60 marks each); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (45 marks each)

papers.paper_name: General Studies Paper III (Part A: Economics - Indian & MP Economy - 150 marks; Part B: Science, Technology & Public Health - 150 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each Part (A and B) for General candidates (60 marks each); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (45 marks each)

papers.paper_name: General Studies Paper IV (Part A: Philosophy, Psychology & Public Administration - 150 marks; Part B: Entrepreneurship, Management & Personality Development - 150 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% in each Part (A and B) for General candidates (60 marks each); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (45 marks each)

papers.paper_name: Paper V: General Hindi & Grammar (सामान्य हिन्दी एवं व्याकरण)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% for General candidates (80 marks); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (60 marks)

papers.paper_name: Paper VI: Hindi Essay & Draft Writing (हिन्दी निबंध एवं प्रारूप लेखन — Essay 1: 50 marks; Essay 2: 20 marks; Draft 1: 15 marks; Report 2: 15 marks)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 40% for General candidates (40 marks); 30% for SC/ST/OBC/EWS/PwD (30 marks)

stages.source_label: MPPSC Vigyapti No. 05-01/2025/Chayan-9: Revised Exam Plan & Syllabus State Service Examination 2026

financial_package.note: Posts recruited through MPPSC State Service Examination are compensated under the Madhya Pradesh Revised Pay Rules, 2017 (MP 7th CPC Pay Matrix). The premier state administrative posts (Deputy Collector / SDM and Deputy Superintendent of Police) start at MP Pay Matrix Level 10 (Pay Band 3: ₹15,600 - 39,100, Grade Pay ₹5,400) with entry basic pay of ₹56,100. Subordinate posts such as Naib Tehsildar start at Pay Matrix Level 9 (Grade Pay ₹3,600, entry basic ₹36,200).
financial_package.pay_source_label: MPPSC Advt. No. 29/2025: State Service Examination 2026 Notification, General Administration Department Post Schedule & MP Revised Pay Rules 2017
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated based on MP Pay Matrix Level 10 entry basic pay of ₹56,100 at 58% DA (effective 1 Jul 2025) and municipal HRA ranging from 8% to 16% (Bhopal/Indore Class Y cities at 16%, other district headquarters at 8-10%); deductions include NPS (10% on Basic+DA = ₹8,864), Professional Tax (₹208), and state group insurance.
official_perks: Government residential bungalow / accommodation allotted from district administrative pool
Official government vehicle with driver for administrative inspections and protocol duty
Armed police escort / security personnel for executive magistrate duties
Subsidized telephone, electricity, and official utilities reimbursement
Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and leave encashment under MP Civil Services Rules
Comprehensive medical reimbursement coverage under MP State Government Employees Scheme
